t: Two rods of the same length and diameter having thermal conductivities K₁ and K₂ are joined in parallel. The equivalent thermal conductivity of the combination is

In parallel combination, the equivalent thermal conductivity is given by
K=(K₁A₁+K₂A₂+K₃A₃+……+KₙAₙ)/(A₁+A₂+A₃+……+Aₙ)
For two rods of equal area, K=((K₁+K₂)A)/2A  (if A₁=A₂=A)
⇒K=(K₁+K₂)/2

t:
A uniform metal ring with centre C have two points A and B, such that angle ACB is θ.A
and B are maintained at two different constant temperatures. If the angle between A and B,
i.e., θ=180°, the rate of heat flow from A to B is 1.2W, then what will be the rate, when θ
=90°
s:
Let ΔT= temperature difference between the rings.
R= total thermal resistance of the ring.
When θ=180° the resistances will be R/2,R/2 and both are in parallel, so equivalent
resistance =R/4
Rate of total heat flow =Q₁/t=1.2=ΔT/(R/4) 0.3=ΔT/R
When θ=90° there are two sections, with resistances, R/4 and 3R/4 in parallel.
So, equivalent resistance =3R/16
Rate of heat flow =Q₂/t=ΔT/(3R/16)
=16/3=(ΔT/R)
=16/3×0.3 W =1.6 W

According to principle of calorimetry. Heat lost by warm water = Heat gained by cold water + Heat gained by the calorimeter [ ⇒ m₂(T₂−T₃)=m₁(T₃−T₁)+W(T₃−T₁); ⇒ 300(60−40)=500(40−30)+W(40−30); ⇒ 300×20=500×10+10W; ⇒ 6000=5000+10W; ⇒ 10W=6000−5000⇒10W=1000; ⇒ W=100 g=100/1000=0.1 kg]

t: 1 kg ice at −20°C is mixed with 1 kg steam at 200°C. Find the mass of water after mixing.
s:
Let equilibrium temperature be 100°C, heat required to convert 1 kg ice at −20°C to 1 kg water at 100°C is equal to
H₁=1×1/2×20+1×80+1×1×100=190kcal
Heat released by steam to convert 1 kg steam at 200°C to 1 kg water at 100°C is equal to
H₂=1×1/2×100+1×540=590kcal
1kg ice at −20°C=H₁+1 kg water at 100°C …(i)
1 kg steam at 200°C=H₂+1 kg water at 100°C …(ii)
By adding Eqs. (i) and (ii)
1 kg ice at −20°C+1 kg steam at 200°C=H₁+H₂+2 kg water at 100°C.
Here heat required to ice is less than heat supplied by steam, so mixture equilibrium temperature is 100°C. Then steam is not completely converted into water.
So mixture has water and steam, which is possible only at 100°C. Mass of steam which converted into water is equal to
m=(190−1×1/2×100)/540=7/27 kg
So mixture content Mass of steam =1−7/27=20/27 kg
Mass of water =1+7/27=34/27 kg .

t: The density of water at 4°C is 1000.0 kg/m³ and at 100°C it is 958.4 kg/m³. The cubic expansivity of water between these temperatures is

i.e., (V−V₀)/V₀1/Δθ=α
α=(m/d₂−m/d₁)/(m/d₁)⋅1/Δθ=(d₁−d₂)/(d₁d₂)×d₁/Δθ
=(d₁−d₂)/d₂⋅1/Δθ=(1000−958.4)/(958.4×96)
=4.5×10⁻⁴ per degree K

t: The energy spectrum of a black body exhibits a maximum around a wavelength λ₀. The temperature of the black body is now changed such that the energy is maximum around a wavelength 3λ₀/4. The power radiated by the black body will now increase by a factor of
s:
According to Wien’s law, wavelength corresponding to maximum energy decreases. When the temperature of black body increases, i.e., λₘT= constant
⇒T₂/T₁=λ₁/λ₂=λ₀/(3λ₀/4)=4/3
Now according to Stefan’s law
E₂/E₁=(T₂/T₁)⁴=(4/3)⁴=256/81

t: 2 kg of ice at −15°C is mixed with 2.5 kg of water at 25°C in an insulating container. If the specific heat capacities of ice and water are 0.5cal/g°C and lcal/g°C, find the amount of water present in the container? (in kg nearest integer)
s:
Energy released by water from 25°C to 0°C=2500×1×25=62500cal
Energy to bring ice 0⁰C
=2000×1/2×15=15000cal
Energy used to melt ice of m gram =m80cal ∴ Ice melt m=((62500−15000)/80)=593.75 g
So, mass of water =(2500+593.75)g =3093.75≃3 kg

t: 2 kg of ice at −20°C is mixed with 5 kg of water at 20°C in an insulating vessel having a negligible heat capacity. Calculate the final mass of water (in kg) remaining in the container.
s:
Energy with 5 kg of H₂O at 20°C to become ice at 0°C
E₁=5000×1×20=100000cal
Energy to raise the temperature of 2 kg ice from −20°C to 0°C
E₁=5000×0.5×20=20000cal
(E₁−E₂)=80000cal is available to melt ice at 0°C. So only 1000 g or 1 kg of ice would have melt.
So, the amount of water available 1+5=6 kg.

t: A brass rod and a lead rod each 80 cm long at 0°C are clamped together at one end with their free ends coinciding. The separation of free ends of the rods if the system is placed in a steam bath is (α_(brass)=18×10⁻⁶/​°C and α_(lead)=28×10⁻⁶/​°C) to the nearest value (in mm) is
s:
The brass rod and the lead rod will suffer expansion when placed in steam bath.
∴ Length of brass rod at 100°C.
Lₜᵣₐₘ=Lₜᵣₐₙ(1+αₜᵣₘΔT)=80[1+18×10⁻⁶×100]
and the length of lead rod at 100°C
L_(kad)=L_(cad)(1+αₗₑₛₛΔT)=80[1+28×10⁻⁶×100]
Separation of free ends of the rods after heating = Lₗₑₐₜ−Lₛₑₙₛ=80[28−18]×10⁻⁴=8×10⁻² cm=0.8 mm
